GEO · AI search operations

Generative engine optimization starts with evidence AI search can find.

Tenten organizes buyer questions, first-party evidence, entity relationships and editorial ownership into a maintained source system. The work improves what AI search can find and understand; each platform decides what it cites.

Schedule your discovery call
See client work

WORKING ARTIFACT

Query landscape
Decision view

COMPARE

Which approach fits our situation?

Product facts, constraints, alternatives, and a canonical owner.

VERIFY

What evidence supports the claim?

Named cases, first-party documents, dates, and review status.

ACT

What should the buyer do next?

A clear decision path, responsibilities, and a real destination.

Priority requires a useful buyer decision, an accountable source, and a human reviewer.

Direct answer

What is generative engine optimization (GEO)?

Generative engine optimization (GEO) makes a brand's useful, source-backed information easier for AI-supported search to discover, understand, and select. For Google Search, this remains SEO: AI Overviews and AI Mode use the core ranking and quality systems, so a page must still be crawlable, indexable, helpful, and eligible for a search snippet. Tenten applies that principle through buyer-question research, first-party evidence, clear entity relationships, maintained pages, and dated citation observations. We do not promise inclusion or claim control over what any AI system cites.

FOUNDATION
Useful non-commodity content, clear technical structure, and maintained evidence.
OBSERVATION
Record the platform, prompt, answer, cited sources, date, and limitations.
Primary source: Google Search Central's generative AI search guide
↗

Point of view

Maintain source-backed answers with clear approval owners.

Start with the buyer questions that matter, the evidence that supports each answer, its page location and its approval owner. Keep facts, names and relationships consistent.

RULE 01

Evidence before copy

A claim enters a draft only when its source, date, and owner are visible.

RULE 02

One entity, one meaning

Names, relationships, and canonical pages stay consistent across the site and distribution channels.

RULE 03

Observe, then decide

AI answers are recorded as dated observations. They are not treated as a permanent rank or a causal result.

RULE 04

Humans approve publication

A named editor and subject owner review facts, framing, and destinations before anything goes live.

The operating system

Seven linked decisions from question to learning.

Each stage leaves a reviewable artifact. Human approval sits inside the workflow, while citation checks remain dated observations that guide the next decision.

01

DECISION

Query landscape

Which buyer questions matter enough to earn a maintained answer?

Artifact: Intent, market, decision stage, source gap, and priority.

HUMAN GATE

The client owner confirms business relevance.

02

DECISION

Source evidence

Which claims can the organization support today?

Artifact: Source URL or document, date checked, claim status, and evidence owner.

HUMAN GATE

A subject-matter owner confirms the facts and permitted use.

03

DECISION

Content and entity architecture

Where should each answer live, and how should entities connect?

Artifact: Canonical pages, entity relationships, question clusters, internal links, and structured-data opportunities.

HUMAN GATE

Brand and web owners approve names, relationships, and destinations.

04

DECISION

Editorial production

What is the clearest complete answer the evidence supports?

Artifact: A source-linked brief and draft with unresolved points left visible.

HUMAN GATE

The editor and subject owner approve the language.

05

DECISION

Publication and distribution

Which owned destinations deserve this answer, and in what form?

Artifact: A live-page checklist plus approved web, newsletter, social, or video packages.

HUMAN GATE

The page owner signs off the live URL and each reuse context.

06

DECISION

Citation observation

What did selected AI surfaces answer and cite on the observation date?

Artifact: Platform, prompt, date, answer summary, cited sources, and visible gaps.

HUMAN GATE

The analyst labels the record as observation, not ranking proof.

07

DECISION

Learning log

What should stay, change, be investigated, or be retired next?

Artifact: Change history, evidence behind the decision, owner, and next review point.

HUMAN GATE

Tenten and the client approve the next action before the cycle repeats.

Reviewable artifacts

Review source, publication and citation observation records.

The records show why a topic was chosen, its supporting evidence, approval owner, published content and subsequent observations, so the team can review decisions and learning.

ARTIFACT

WHAT MUST BE VISIBLE

OWNER

Query landscape

Buyer question, intent, market, decision stage, source gap, and priority rationale.

Growth or marketing owner

Evidence register

Claim, first-party or named source, date checked, confidence, usage note, and subject owner.

Subject-matter owner

Entity and content map

Canonical entity names, relationships, destination pages, question clusters, and internal links.

Brand and web owners

Publication record

Approved draft, reviewer, live URL, release date, distribution variants, and change note.

Editor and page owner

Citation observation log

Dated prompt, platform, answer summary, cited URLs, absent sources, and limitations.

GEO analyst

Learning log

Observed change, plausible explanation, evidence, decision, next action, and review owner.

Client and Tenten leads

Editorial and distribution experience

Owned AI media keeps us close to the publishing work.

Tenten operates its own AI-focused editorial channels. We use that experience to shape questions, review evidence, adapt approved material for different formats, and keep distribution tied to the same source record. It is editorial experience, not a shortcut to an AI outcome.

01

Editorial judgment

Operating owned AI media gives our team direct experience choosing useful questions, editing source-backed answers, and maintaining a coherent point of view.

02

Distribution packaging

One approved source can become a web page, newsletter, social post, or video only when its evidence and context still hold in the new format.

03

Feedback discipline

Channel response and citation observations feed the learning log. Neither is presented as proof that one publication caused a business result.

Named case evidence

Neteon: Webflow redesign, SEO and HubSpot CRM

For Neteon, Tenten rebuilt the website in Webflow, improved SEO and connected HubSpot CRM for contact tracking and follow-up. The named case reports an 86%+ search-ranking gain after that work; this is not a forecast or minimum for other brands.

86%+
SEO ranking gain reported for the named Neteon revamp case.
Case scope
Webflow redesign, SEO improvements, and HubSpot CRM integration.
Read the Neteon case study →

Fit and trade-offs

This works when the organization can own the source with us.

GOOD FIT

Your team has real expertise and is ready to make its evidence, decisions, and approvals maintainable.

Your expertise exists, but it is scattered

Product pages, PDFs, sales decks, and specialist knowledge do not yet form one maintained source system.

You can name the reviewers

Marketing, product, legal, or subject experts can approve facts and explain where uncertainty remains.

You want a durable publishing operation

The goal is to improve source quality and decision usefulness across the site and owned channels, then learn from observation.

TRADE-OFFS

The system favors source quality, explicit ownership, and careful observation over volume or certainty theatre.

No fixed content quota

Output follows the query landscape and available evidence. A quota can create pages that add no useful answer.

No controlled AI outcome

No agency controls whether an AI system cites or orders a source. We improve the source system and document what selected surfaces show.

Approval is real work

The client supplies source access and named reviewers. Tenten keeps the evidence, drafts, publication records, and learning log moving.

Next step

Review buyer questions, existing evidence and approvals.

Bring the buyer questions that matter, the sources you trust and the people who approve facts and publication. We use those inputs to discuss source maintenance, publishing requirements and whether the engagement fits.

Shopify Partner / Commerce delivery

Build a Shopify storefront your team can run.

Tenten is a Shopify Partner. We plan your catalog, markets, checkout, apps, integrations, measurement, and operations before building the storefront.

Contact us
Review the operating system

INPUT
Catalog + markets

DECISIONS
Checkout + systems

RECEIPTS
Release + handoff

Concept image. The records below define scope; the portfolio shows inspectable work.

Commerce operating system

Review the Shopify build plan.

Each part of the build has a decision to approve, evidence to review, and a named owner.

01

Model

Catalog + content model

What is a product, a variant, a collection, and reusable product content?

Use a variant only when an option changes the sellable item or its operational data.
Store reusable editorial facts once, then reference them instead of copying them across products.
REVIEW ARTIFACT
Field map, sample product, and migration transform
OWNERSHIP
Tenten drafts; merchant approves product semantics

02

Markets

Market + localization matrix

Which commercial rule changes by country, region, language, or currency?

Create a market rule when price, tax, payment, delivery, availability, or legal copy changes.
A translation alone does not create a second product record unless operations require one.
REVIEW ARTIFACT
Market matrix with URLs, currency, language, availability, and owner
OWNERSHIP
Merchant owns commercial policy; Tenten maps it to the storefront

03

Checkout

Checkout + app decision log

Can the requirement stay native, or does it justify another dependency?

Start with Shopify and theme capabilities; add an app only against a named requirement.
Verify current plan eligibility before promising a checkout change, then record cost, data access, and an exit path.
REVIEW ARTIFACT
Decision log with requirement, chosen path, trade-off, approver, and review date
OWNERSHIP
Tenten recommends; merchant approves recurring cost and vendor dependency

04

Systems

Integration inventory

Which system writes each field, and what happens when an exchange fails?

Name one source of truth per field and document direction, trigger, identifier, retry, and exception handling.
Do not let two systems write the same value without a conflict rule and a human owner.
REVIEW ARTIFACT
System inventory and sample payload or file for every integration in scope
OWNERSHIP
Each system has a business owner and a technical escalation owner

05

Measurement

Analytics event contract

What user action creates each event, and how will the team prove it arrived?

Define the trigger, required commerce fields, consent condition, destination, and test method before tagging.
Accept purchase only when the test order carries a unique transaction ID and does not duplicate on reload.
REVIEW ARTIFACT
Event map plus browser, analytics, and order read-back for the approved test path
OWNERSHIP
Growth owns meaning; Tenten owns implementation in scope

06

Release

Launch reconciliation

What changed between the approved baseline and the release candidate?

Compare catalog, market, redirect, checkout, integration, and event records at the release boundary.
Log every variance with a disposition and owner before the go-live decision.
REVIEW ARTIFACT
Dated reconciliation sheet tied to the release candidate
OWNERSHIP
Tenten runs the review; merchant accepts commercial exceptions

07

Operations

Editor + operations handoff

Can the people running the store complete routine work and recognize an exception?

Train against real tasks: edit a product, publish content, change availability, inspect an order, and find an event receipt.
Separate routine changes, approval-only changes, and issues that require escalation.
REVIEW ARTIFACT
Recorded scenarios, role map, runbook, and open-issue register
OWNERSHIP
Merchant names operators; Tenten transfers the agreed workflow

Decision workbench

Plan the catalog, markets, and checkout.

Approve product fields, market rules, and checkout requirements before we build the storefront.

RECORD 01 / CATALOG MODEL

One field map, four different jobs.

The merchant approves the meaning before migration or entry begins.

Product

One merchandising identity and shared product story

Split only when buyers, operations, or reporting need a separate item.

Variant

A sellable option with its own SKU, price, inventory, weight, or fulfilment rule

Do not use variants as a content-layout shortcut.

Collection

A merchandising or navigation set

Record whether membership is manual, rule-based, or market-specific.

Reusable content

Ingredients, materials, care, size guidance, campaign modules, or other shared facts

Model once and reference it; name the editor responsible for updates.

RECORD 02 / MARKET MATRIX

Localization follows the commercial rule.

01

Price, currency, tax, or payment changes

Create an explicit commercial rule for that market.

ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE

Approved price source, tax owner, payment provider, and checkout test.

02

Language changes but the offer does not

Localize the shared record and keep one product identity.

ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE

Locale field map, fallback behavior, and editor assignment.

03

Availability or fulfilment changes

Define where the product can be seen, bought, and delivered.

ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE

Market-product matrix and shipping scenario receipt.

RECORD 03 / CHECKOUT AND APP LOG

Every dependency needs a reason and an exit.

Merchandising or content change

Theme or admin configuration

No app unless the requirement cannot be met cleanly in the owned build.

Checkout behavior change

Current Shopify capability first

Confirm plan eligibility and test boundary before scope approval.

Third-party app

Named requirement and owner

Record recurring cost, permissions, data path, support owner, and replacement path.

Custom service

Use only when business logic cannot live safely in the storefront

Document hosting, monitoring, failure behavior, and maintenance ownership.

Records 04 + 05

Connect systems and verify analytics.

Document each integration's data source and responsible owner. Verify each analytics event's trigger, payload, destination, and test result.

INTEGRATION INVENTORY

One owner per exchange boundary

Product source

Failure owner: Merchandising operations

OWNS
Product IDs, variants, approved copy, and media
EXCHANGE
Approved publish or migration transform into Shopify

ERP / fulfilment

Failure owner: Operations plus integration owner

OWNS
Inventory, order, shipment, and cancellation fields named in scope
EXCHANGE
API, webhook, or batch with identifiers and retry rules

CRM / lifecycle messaging

Failure owner: Marketing operations

OWNS
Consented customer and order signals approved for activation
EXCHANGE
Event or batch, with field-level consent and deletion rules

Analytics

Failure owner: Growth owner plus implementation owner

OWNS
Event meaning, commerce parameters, and destination mapping
EXCHANGE
Browser or server path recorded per event

ANALYTICS EVENT CONTRACT

Trigger, fields, destination, proof

01

view_item

A product detail view resolves with the agreed stable product or variant ID.

Receipt: Debug payload matches the visible item and market.

02

add_to_cart

The cart accepts the selected item and quantity.

Receipt: Payload and cart state agree on item ID, quantity, price, and currency.

03

begin_checkout

The buyer leaves the cart for checkout, not when the cart merely opens.

Receipt: One event for the tested transition with the agreed cart fields.

04

purchase

The approved order confirmation is available.

Receipt: Unique transaction ID, value, currency, items, and a reload deduplication check.

05

search

The storefront returns results for a non-sensitive query.

Receipt: Query and result state are readable without collecting personal data.

Records 06 + 07

Launch is a reconciliation. Handoff is a working session.

The release candidate is checked against the approved baseline. Operators then complete real store tasks and leave with a runbook and escalation path.

LAUNCH RECONCILIATION

Catalog
Product and variant counts
Collection membership
Media and reusable fields
Markets
Language and currency
Availability and delivery
Market URLs and fallbacks
Checkout
Payment test
Tax and shipping scenarios
Discount, refund, and cancellation path
Continuity
Redirect map
Metadata and indexability
Analytics event and test-order receipts
Integrations
Sent and received IDs
Exception log
Retry and escalation owner
Operations
Editor scenarios
Permissions
Runbook and open-issue register

EDITOR AND OPERATIONS HANDOFF

The operator does the work
01

Create or update a product with variants, media, reusable content, and search fields.

02

Publish a collection or campaign change using the approved review path.

03

Apply a market-specific availability or content change without altering another market.

04

Find an order, identify its integration status, and follow the exception path.

05

Run an analytics test and locate the event and order receipts.

06

Revert or escalate a change using the runbook instead of relying on one developer's memory.

Inspectable commerce work

Commerce websites we have built.

Explore airport pre-order commerce, regional storefront operations, and direct e-commerce work for Everrich Duty Free, SMALO Ebikes, and Wahuda Tools.

Pre-order commerce for airport collection

Everrich Duty Free

Browse, tax handling, checkout, and the first-time buyer explanation are documented in the case.

Inspect the case →

Regional storefront and operations

Fit, trade-off, ownership

The platform decision is part of scope, not a foregone conclusion.

GOOD FIT WHEN

The catalog, variants, markets, and fulfilment rules can be made explicit.
The merchant team wants Shopify admin to be a primary operating surface.
App and integration dependencies can have named budgets, owners, and exit paths.
Checkout requirements can be accepted only after current capability and plan checks.

TRADE-OFFS TO ACCEPT

A specialized configurator, marketplace, or back-office workflow may need a separate service and maintenance boundary.
Every app adds recurring cost, permissions, data movement, vendor support, and upgrade work.
Each additional market multiplies policy decisions and release scenarios. Localization also changes operations.
A migration needs explicit URL, content, event, and order checks; platform movement alone does not preserve them.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY

A clear build has no invisible owner

Approves commercial rules, recurring costs, release exceptions, and go-live

Shopify and app vendors

Their platform, product behavior, service terms, and vendor support

External dependencies remain visible in the inventory and escalation plan

MANAGED WORDPRESS HOSTING

Managed WordPress hosting with clear responsibilities.

Before we take access, we document the server scope, backups and restore checks, update approvals, monitoring and escalation, incident decisions, and handoff responsibilities.

Get a free estimate
Review the control model
Responsibility matrix
Restore evidence
Change record
Rollback decision
Access handoff
OPERATING MODEL
SCOPE FIRST
Concept image of hosting operations. The written scope defines the responsibilities for your site.

Responsibility matrix

Managed does not mean invisible.

The proposal names the platform, Tenten and client owners for each boundary. If ownership changes, the matrix changes before access or production work does.

CONTROL BOUNDARY
TENTEN
YOUR TEAM
EVIDENCE RETAINED

01

Cloud account and billing

Recommend an option and document the access needed for the agreed scope.

Own the commercial account and approve spend unless the proposal says otherwise.

Account owner, billing contact, access boundary

02

Server baseline

Record the runtime, configuration, dependencies and known constraints before change work starts.

Confirm the production site, business critical periods and people who can approve risk.

Baseline inventory, scope, approver

03

WordPress and PHP changes

Assess compatibility, record versions and execute an approved change window. Use staging when it exists and is included.

Provide valid plugin licenses, acceptance criteria and a decision owner for functional risk.

Change record, checks, rollback condition

04

Backups and restore

Run the agreed schedule and retain the job and restore evidence included in scope.

Confirm data criticality, retention needs and the acceptable recovery trade-off.

Backup result, restore test, timestamp

05

Monitoring and escalation

Configure the agreed checks, validate alerts and open the documented escalation path.

Keep business contacts current and decide when impact calls for customer communication or a trade-off.

Signal, threshold, channel, decision owner

06

Domain, DNS and third parties

Make only approved changes inside the agreed control boundary.

Retain ownership and recovery access for the registrar, DNS, email and connected services.

System owner, recovery path, approved change

07

Data, content and compliance

Protect granted access and follow the data handling boundary written into the engagement.

Own lawful processing, content accuracy, retention decisions and regulatory approval.

Data boundary, access list, client approval

08

Incident and rollback

Record the timeline, contain the issue and recommend a forward fix or rollback from the available evidence.

Approve business trade-offs when recovery time, data loss or customer impact differs between options.

Incident timeline, decision, recovery checks

Minimum evidence pack

Records for backups, updates, incidents and handoff.

These examples cover restore checks, approved changes, monitoring, incident decisions and access handoff. Your written scope confirms which records Tenten will create, retain and transfer; they are not completed records from your site.

01

REQUIRED RECORD

Backup and restore evidence

Can this site be recovered from a known point?

Agreed schedule and retention
Files and database job result
Restore target, result and timestamp
Gap or exception that still needs an owner

A successful backup job is not the same as a successful restore test.

02

REQUIRED RECORD

Update and change record

Is this change understood, approved and reversible enough to run?

Request, owner and affected versions
Risk and maintenance window
Pre-change and post-change checks
Rollback condition and known-good point

Updates are assessed changes. Custom code and plugins can make unattended updates unsafe.

03

REQUIRED RECORD

Monitoring and escalation map

Who receives the signal, validates impact and makes the next decision?

Endpoint or resource being checked
Signal and alert condition
Primary and backup escalation channels
Business decision owner

Monitoring can detect a symptom. It does not guarantee availability or resolve the cause.

04

REQUIRED RECORD

Incident and rollback record

Do we contain, fix forward, restore or roll back?

Timeline and observed impact
Recent changes and working hypothesis
Decision owner and containment action
Recovery checks and follow-up owner

Rollback is conditional. Data changes and third-party failures may need a different recovery path.

05

REQUIRED RECORD

Access and handoff pack

Can the next owner operate the site without hidden access or context?

Account and system inventory
Named owners and access level
Runbook, open risks and next window
Credential transfer, rotation or revocation

The client keeps recoverable ownership. Secrets stay in an approved credential store, not in the runbook.

Operating decisions

Five gates before the next action.

A runbook should make the stop, approve, escalate and handoff points visible. It should not turn every alert into the same answer.

01

Before migration

If there is no named owner, required access or usable recovery point, resolve that gap before scheduling cutover.

RECORD: OWNER LIST, ACCESS CHECK, BASELINE AND RECOVERY POINT

02

Before a planned change

Record the risk, approver, window, checks and rollback condition. Use an available staging path when it is compatible and included.

RECORD: APPROVED CHANGE RECORD

03

When an alert fires

Validate user impact and recent changes, then escalate through the agreed channel. Do not treat the alert itself as a diagnosis.

RECORD: ALERT EVIDENCE AND TRIAGE NOTE

04

During an incident

Contain first. Choose a forward fix, restore or rollback against the known-good state, data risk and business impact.

RECORD: INCIDENT TIMELINE AND RECOVERY DECISION

05

At handoff

Transfer the inventory, open risks, access boundary and next maintenance window. Rotate or revoke access as agreed.

RECORD: SIGNED-OFF HANDOFF PACK

Infrastructure options

Choose AWS, GCE or Azure for your operating requirements.

We confirm account ownership, region, required services, support and exit requirements before selecting a provider. Availability and performance depend on the provider and the agreed scope.

OPTION 01

AWS

Amazon Web Services. Availability and fit are confirmed against the actual account and scope.

OPTION 02

GCE

Google Compute Engine. Availability and fit are confirmed against the actual account and scope.

OPTION 03

Azure

Microsoft Azure. Availability and fit are confirmed against the actual account and scope.

PROVIDER DECISION INPUTS

01
Existing account ownership and procurement
02
Required region and service availability
03
Current architecture and migration constraints
04
Budget, provider support and account responsibilities
05
Exit, recovery and handoff requirements

Fit and trade-offs

Useful when ownership matters. Wrong when certainty is being sold as a feature.
Good fit
A WordPress site with named technical and business decision owners.
A team that wants recurring maintenance backed by written change and recovery records.
An organization that can provide recoverable provider, WordPress, registrar and DNS access.
A team prepared to use maintenance windows, acceptance checks and explicit approval for risk.
A buyer who values a clear handoff and continued client ownership of the accounts.
Not a fit
A requirement for uninterrupted availability, zero incidents or universal performance gains.
An expectation that every core, PHP, theme and plugin update runs without compatibility review.
A setup with no client-side account owner, recovery access or business decision contact.
A regulated or certified operating requirement that has not been separately reviewed and written into scope.
A one-time speed repair with no ongoing hosting need. That should be scoped as performance work instead.

SCOPE BOUNDARY

What this page does not promise
Cloud provider outages, credits and regional service terms remain subject to the selected provider.
Monitoring coverage and response channels are defined in the proposal. Monitoring does not mean continuous human observation or guaranteed uptime.
Backups reduce recovery risk, but recovery depends on retention, restore testing, data timing and the failure mode.
Security controls reduce exposure. They do not make WordPress, custom code or third-party services incident-free.
Plugin licenses, custom application work, DNS or email ownership, compliance review and specific recovery objectives are included only when written into scope.

SCOPE THE OPERATING CONTRACT

Bring the current host, access map and recovery questions.

We will identify the missing decisions, confirm what Tenten can own, and put the responsibilities, evidence and exclusions into the estimate.

HEADLESS CMS / JAMSTACK

One content system for every digital touchpoint.

Store content once and deliver it to websites, apps, commerce, and other channels through APIs. We own the model, front end, migration, integrations, and launch.

Schedule your discovery call
See selected work
React

Custom APIs
The final platform choice follows the content, team, and integration requirements.

Why headless

One content repository, any frontend

A headless CMS separates content (the body) from its presentation (the head). Editors work in one repository; sites, apps and screens retrieve content through APIs. The CMS, frontend and infrastructure need separate ownership, adding complexity compared with an all-in-one CMS.

One source of truth
Manage website, app, commerce, and internal content together, then publish through documented APIs.
Editors and engineers work in parallel
The content model gives each team a contract, so editorial work does not wait for every frontend release.
A frontend can change without moving the archive
A new site or channel can use the existing content APIs when the model still fits the job.

Architecture decision

Choose headless for the operating model, not the label

Headless earns its extra moving parts when several products, markets, or teams need the same structured content. For one website with a simple editing workflow, an integrated CMS is often the better system.

Integrated CMS

Best fit

One primary website, a small editing team, and few custom integrations

Operating model

One platform owns content, templates, preview, and hosting

Trade-off

Harder to reuse the same content across products or replace the presentation layer

Headless CMS

Best fit

Several frontends, structured content reuse, complex permissions, or deep integrations

Operating model

CMS, frontend development, and infrastructure are separate responsibilities

Trade-off

More architecture, testing, and operational ownership than an all-in-one CMS

Migration workbench

The estimate is built from these four inspectable artifacts.

01
Inventory

Content types, locales, media, URLs, integrations, and ownership

02
Model

Fields, references, permissions, preview, validation, and API contracts

03

04
Cut over

Parity QA, editor acceptance, monitoring, rollback, and launch receipt

Not every case proves the same thing

We label direct technology proof, adjacent operating experience, and portfolio context separately. That is more useful than calling all three logos headless projects.
